keyFindings.text: **DRIFT (P1) — the notes' loop-ask gate no longer matches the Python fallback at HEAD.** Notes lines 494-513 claim the advisor attaches a deep command to an iteration count of two or more, a named loop, a want before a loop name, a continuation, and so on. `73d98332fff` (2026-11-25, `refactor(system-skill-advisor): keep a fallback deep-loop row only when its command is typed`) deleted about 1,300 lines of the Python fallback's own offer gate, and at HEAD `_apply_deep_loop_offer_gate` keeps a `/deep:research`, `/deep:review` or `/doctor:deep-loop` row only when the prompt types that command. That commit is one of six that landed after the notes' last edit (`98b712cd248`), so the claim is stale for the fallback path the notes do not distinguish. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/skill_advisor.py:4602] [SOURCE: .skilled/changelog/skilled/v4.2.0.0.md:494]

keyFindings.text: **BUG (P2) — the `typed` mark is dropped when the run row is normalized onto an existing owner row.** `_apply_deep_loop_offer_gate` sets `rec["typed"] = True` on a run row whose command the reader typed (`skill_advisor.py:4624`), and the comment above the row tables states that "the renamed row carries the typed mark on to the owning skill" (`skill_advisor.py:4562`). `normalize_command_bridge_recommendations` then builds `normalized = dict(owner or top)` and copies `confidence`, `uncertainty`, `passes_threshold`, `_kind_priority` and `_explicit_skill_match` from the top row — but never `typed` (`skill_advisor.py:3338-3362`). When the owning skill row is already present, `normalized` starts from that row and the typed mark is lost; when it is absent, `dict(top)` keeps it. No in-repo consumer reads the field, so the impact is output fidelity and a comment that states a behavior the code does not have. Introduced by `73d98332fff`. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/skill_advisor.py:3338] [SOURCE: .skilled/changelog/skilled/v4.2.0.0.md:494]

The twenty-first test, `the status remedy quotes a tree root with a space so it runs as pasted`, landed in `3bfd5e111fc` on 2026-11-21, four days before the notes' last edit (`98b712cd248`, 2026-11-25), so the row was wrong at writing time rather than outrun by later work. ruledOutDirections.text: **Count drift.** "14 skills" matches the 14 tracked top-level `SKILL.md` files; "seventeen" doctor commands matches the 17 `*.md` files under `.skilled/commands/doctor/`; the `/doctor:setup` target table has exactly 26 rows; `/doctor:skill-advisor` lists 6 targets; the advisor lockfile has 111 packages and the spec-kit lockfile 313, matching the notes' cost block.

**Counting the Python scorer tests from source.** The fallback test file has 22 `def test_` functions but runs case tables, so 130 and 138 cannot be reconciled by counting. Deferred to a later iteration with a direct suite run or a test-record source.

**Deep Loop section drift.** Every sampled claim held: `--depth-mode=expansive` and both frontier cap flags are documented in `.skilled/commands/deep/research.md:3,109-111` and `review.md:3,102-104`; the frontier defaults are 3 deep and 6 children; the budget split is 50/35/15; the blocked thresholds are 2 for review and 3 for research (`convergence.cjs:1595`, `deep-review-config.json:23`, `deep-research-config.json:17`); `blockedStop` is emitted (`convergence.cjs:1177`); and the `blocked_stop` row exists (`convergence.cjs:1511`).

**Dispatch section drift.** The 20 MB cap and `ENOBUFS` verdict exist (`executor-audit.ts:1515`, `fanout-run.cjs:5853`); `iterations/iteration-NNN.cost.json` is written with `providerCostUsd` (`dispatch-iteration.cjs:451,472`); and `SPECKIT_ALLOW_HOST_SESSION_EXECUTOR` relaxes only ancestry and env (`executor-audit.ts:42`).

**Fan-Out section drift.** `--status`, `--stop` and `--only-lineage` exist (`fanout-run.cjs:37,1526,2021`); a one-lineage matrix is refused (`fanout-run.cjs:4944`); a native lineage is refused (`fanout-run.cjs:4649`); the stop grace is 2,500 ms (`fanout-run.cjs:1463`); `survivors` is returned (`fanout-run.cjs:1536`); and `provider_cost_usd` is emitted (`fanout-run.cjs:6142`).

**Removal drift.** `--allow-single-lineage` has no remaining reference; `opencode2` has no reference in the deep-loop runtime; `.skilled/skills/cli-orca` is gone; `dualPlugin` is gone from `v2-bridge.js` (`definePlugin` at line 327); `nativeDual` is gone from `plugin-inventory.json` (`selfRegistered` instead); `.skilled/manual-testing-playbook/` is gone.

**Treating the 10-folder "Spec folders" block as the coverage list.** It lists 10 packets while `recent-packets.txt` holds 21, but the block is metadata, not a coverage claim; the packet-coverage question needs the per-packet check scheduled for a later iteration.
**Anchor or component-list drift.** All 63 internal links resolve, and every named component has a release entry.
**Browser pin drift.** Bladebro v4.8.2, bdg 0.6.10, three modes and eight hubs all match.
**Doctor count drift.** 17 commands, 26 setup rows, 6 advisor targets, 5 install steps and 66 scenarios all match.
**OpenCode drift.** The major-2-only rule, the two-mode helper, the retired launcher names, the 18-subcommand shim and the v2 battery workflow all match HEAD.
**Overlay layout drift.** The notes' layout, relayout, sibling-folder, audit and cache claims match the engine and its reference doc line for line.

**Reconciling 2,450 and 3,557 advisor suite totals.** The rows are labelled differently ("Advisor runtime suite" vs "with the loop offers"), so they may be two suite configurations rather than a contradiction. No HEAD run exists in the packet to settle it; recorded as an observation, not a finding.
**Running the advisor or deep-loop suites to get HEAD counts.** Out of scope: a suite run writes test artifacts outside the lineage directory, which the dispatch forbids.
**`013-deep-loop-offer-in-hint` as a MISSING.** It is unlisted but its shipped behavior is described by the notes' "The Advisor Offers the Loop With Its Flags" section.
**A second sk-git version gap.** `v1.11.14.0` changes only the claim that `create` is idempotent; it is a documentation correction, not user-visible behavior.

**The eight unlisted packets that shipped nothing.** `005-skill-readability-refinement`, `001-hub-routing-quality`, `003-changelog-system`, `007-alignment-lane-runner`, `001-headless-bots-first-build`, `002-session-handover-loop` and `mcp-code-mode` have only `docs(specs)`, `chore(specs)` or `refactor(specs)` commits in the window, so their absence from the notes is correct. `001-headless-bots-first-build`'s own latest child states "Planned, not started."

**Using packet commit counts as a shipping signal without filtering commit types.** The first count said all 21 were touched and suggested several shipped; filtering `docs`/`chore`/`merge` reduced that to nine packets with shipped work. The unfiltered count would have produced false MISSING findings.
**A band budget that carries upward.** `carry` is set from the current band's remainder and applied to the next band only.
**A fan-out stop that records a live lineage as stopped.** The confirmation loop re-reads the process table and filters survivors on every pass until the grace expires.

**A gate that reads rows by the wrong id.** `_DEEP_LOOP_RUN_ROWS` maps only the bridge id, but the gate runs before `normalize_command_bridge_recommendations`, so that is the id the rows carry at that point; the ordering helper runs after and accepts both ids.

**A pass-evidence off-by-one on a same-millisecond commit.** The window uses an exclusive start and an inclusive end, which is correct for sequential commits; a same-millisecond pair yields an empty window, not a misattributed call.
**An incomplete cli-orca removal.** All runtime mirrors and live trees are clean.

**Running the advisor suite or the Python fallback to observe the gate.** Both would write outside the lineage directory (a test artifact or a SQLite file), which the dispatch forbids. The gate's behavior was established by reading the code instead.
**Finding the README-check script behind "79 of 79".** No script in the deep-loop tree reports that count, so the figure stays UNKNOWN.
**Pinned-file-count drift.** The 187-file figure is explicitly pinned to `46465394d97` and matches that commit.
**Plugin-count drift.** The plugin count is exactly 20.

**Running the advisor, deep-loop or doctor suites to settle their totals.** Each writes test artifacts or coverage databases outside the lineage directory, which the dispatch forbids. Those totals stay UNKNOWN with the exact command that would settle them.
**Shared-case drift.** 368 matches.

**The 595-file figure as a tree count.** It does not describe the whole tree, but the notes present it as a quality-gate scope, which the gate computes over a selected file set; calling it drift would be unsupported.

**Reading every one of the 165 `fix(system-deep-loop)` commits in full.** The subject filter plus the notes' folded blocks reduced the set to a handful of clusters; opening all of them would have consumed the budget without a better answer.
**The Pi fix as a DRIFT.** It restores a default the notes never state, so it is a MISSING entry rather than a contradiction.
**The sk-doc hub-vocabulary failure as a separate BUG.** The commit is itself the fix; at HEAD the router and the trigger line agree, so no defect remains.

**Treating every `fix` subject as a MISSING candidate.** Most fix subjects restate behavior the notes already describe in a folded "Smaller fixes" block; only three clusters survived the check against the notes' text.
**A breaking-change item that no longer holds.** All twenty were checked and hold at HEAD.
**A missing entry for a listed component.** Every one of the fourteen named components has changelog commits in the window.
**A wrong cited version.** Both cited versions exist exactly as named.
**Reproducing the "2 of 26 plain loop asks" routing-analysis figure.** No committed corpus carries that slice, so the number stays UNKNOWN rather than contradicted.
**A doctor update that cleans before rebuilding.** The phase order puts the cleanup last.
**A relayout that leaves a half state.** The restore path covers every move, the manifest write and each relink.
**An adopt path that ships a credential file.** Both the `.env` and the token-named refusals run per file before any copy.
**An adopt that writes outside the overlay folder.** The link guard resolves the source and refuses an escape.
**Executing an adopt or relayout against a real tree.** Both write outside the lineage directory, which the dispatch forbids; the refusals were read from the code instead.
Large suite totals (advisor 2,450/3,557, deep-loop 4,039, doctor 1,673+19) and the live cost figures remain UNKNOWN because reproducing them needs a suite run outside the lineage write boundary.
The "2 of 26 plain loop asks" analysis figure has no committed corpus and stays UNKNOWN.
**A missing or duplicated artifact.** Every iteration has exactly one narrative and one delta, and the state log has exactly one record per iteration.
**A stale registry.** The registry's counts match the iteration files.
